style: GitHub-dark profile banner. Minimal, geometric, confident — not a flashy ad. One continuous particle system (small dots) is the entire visual: it assembles into the monogram 'MG', liquifies, and re-forms into a simple rounded chat-bubble silhouette with a small tail (WhatsApp-style icon), then relaxes back toward the opening scatter density so the loop point is seamless. No camera moves, no background elements beyond the dot field on flat #0d1117 — the banner sits behind embedded README text so motion stays calm and centered, nothing crowds the vertical edges.
font: Inter — confirmed in the HF embed list (packages/studio fontCatalog.ts POPULAR_GOOGLE_FONT_FAMILIES; embeddable via the standard HF Google Fonts stylesheet at weights 300–900). Use weight 900 (Inter Black) for the 'MG' glyph the dot-matrix samples — maximum stroke mass gives the cleanest bitmap for grid-sampling at a 400px-tall canvas; 800 (ExtraBold) is an acceptable fallback if 900 reads too dense at the chosen font-size. The draft's placeholder 'Inter (Bold/Black)' is correct as to family — Inter is real and embeddable — this just pins the exact weight and confirms it against the live catalog.

relevant_hits.name: particle-text-dissolve
relevant_hits.verdict: REUSE THE TECHNIQUE, not as a mountable block for this shot — it only drives ONE target set (a single text string's bitmap) per mount/timeline and only knows direction in|out (cloud↔one-text). It is the closest thing in the registry to scene 1's 'MG' assembly: seeded LCG particle table (fixed seed), offscreen-canvas fillText() + getImageData() bitmap sampling into a deterministic grid of lit cells, zero per-particle GSAP tweens, one onUpdate repaint that is a pure function of (table, time). This exact mechanism is the donor for the hand-authored system below.

catalog_search.conclusion: No catalog block or component performs a continuous particle swarm between two different point-cloud targets (a text glyph and an icon silhouette) while preserving one seeded particle table across the whole duration — confirmed gap, matching the draft's own flag. Hand-author one continuous canvas particle system for the full 3.8s, reusing particle-text-dissolve's exact determinism law (fixed-seed LCG, offscreen bitmap sampling, pure one-shot repaint) for the MG target set, and applying that same bitmap-sampling technique to a hand-drawn vector bubble icon (canvas path fill + stroke passes, not fillText) for the bubble target set.

note_for_builder: HAND-AUTHOR per catalog_search above — do not try to mount particle-text-dissolve/particle-image-reveal as separate per-scene clips; that would reset the particle table at each scene boundary and break the 'one continuous dot field' requirement and the loop seam. Build ONE full-bleed <canvas> inside ONE clip spanning the full 0–3.8s, one paused GSAP root timeline, one onUpdate repaint that is a pure function of (particle table, tl.time()) — same determinism law as the two donor components (no Math.random, no requestAnimationFrame, no incremental state; every frame clears and redraws from scratch). See particle_system below for the full technical spec. Loop requirement is strict: this renders as a looping <video> in a GitHub README — paint(0) and paint(3.8) must be identical (not just visually close) by construction (see loop_closure), so there is no hard cut, brightness pop, or color flash at the wrap.

particle_system.mount: Single #root canvas, full-bleed 1920x400, container-type:size, cqmin units for responsive sizing exactly like the donor components. One LCG with a fixed seed (reuse 0x9d1550f7 or pick a new fixed constant — must stay literally fixed, never derived from Date.now()).
particle_system.count: ~1500 particles total (between the donors' 'med' (900–1700) and the needs of a 1920x400 banner at this resolution). Fixed at mount, one row in the particle table per index 0..1499.

target_sets.scatter: t=0 and t=3.8 target (and the thing loop-bridge eases back toward). Per-particle base position is a fixed random (x,y) from the LCG, offset by a small deterministic periodic drift: drift(i,t) = ampl_i * sin(2*PI*t/3.8 + phase_i), where ampl_i and phase_i are drawn once from the LCG per particle. Because the drift's period equals duration_s exactly, drift(i,0) === drift(i,3.8) bit-for-bit — this is what makes the loop seamless by construction, not by eyeballing two frames.
target_sets.mg: Sampled ONCE at mount exactly like particle-text-dissolve: render 'MG' in Inter 900 (fitted to ~70% of canvas height) to an offscreen canvas via fillText, getImageData, grid-sample lit cells (alpha > 127) on a step tuned so ~1500 cells survive the donor's deterministic LCG-thinning (one LCG draw per cell in grid order, exactly as particle-text-dissolve does it). Each particle index i gets target_mg[i] from this set (index-paired 1:1 since both sets are thinned to the same count).
target_sets.bubble: Sampled ONCE at mount via canvas vector drawing (NOT fillText): draw a rounded-rect body (~34cqmin wide x 22cqmin tall, radius ~8cqmin) plus a small triangular/circular tail at lower-left, centered just right of/below the MG position, to the SAME offscreen canvas approach — one pass with ctx.fill() for the body+tail interior, one pass with ctx.stroke() (outline only, ~3px) sampled at a denser grid step than the fill pass. Flag each surviving cell outline:true|false during sampling. Thin to the same ~1500-particle count with the donor's LCG-thinning so target_bubble[i] pairs 1:1 with the same index i used for target_mg[i] and the scatter set.
target_sets.pairing_note: All three target sets are thinned/capped to the identical particle count (~1500) using the same per-cell LCG-draw thinning technique as the donor, so every particle index i carries exactly one (scatter_i, mg_i, bubble_i, outline_flag_i) tuple for the whole duration — this is what lets scenes hand off without re-seeding or re-sampling mid-timeline.

particle_system.loop_closure: paint(0) and paint(3.8) both evaluate to: particle i at position scatter_i with drift(i,0)==drift(i,3.8), at the same dim ambient opacity/color (#a78bfa @ ~25-30% alpha). Because both endpoints read the same closed-form drift function at equal t (mod duration), they are identical, not approximated — the strict loop requirement is satisfied by construction.

palette_per_state.scatter: #a78bfa at ~25-30% opacity, small radius, slow drift only
palette_per_state.mg_hold: #a78bfa core color; the 0.5–1.4s breathing pulse is a single GLOBAL alpha multiplier (sine, ±8%, one cycle) applied to the whole field — not per-particle random flicker
palette_per_state.bubble_outline: #c4b5fd, higher opacity (~90%), denser sampling — reads crisply at small README width
palette_per_state.bubble_fill: #a78bfa, lower opacity (~45%), sparser sampling — fill is a suggestion of volume, outline carries the silhouette
palette_per_state.background: #0d1117 solid fill behind the canvas, no gradient

scenes.emotion: quiet confidence, a quick snap into focus
scenes.motion: [0.00-0.50s] Every particle eases from its scatter_i/drift position toward target_mg[i] (ease power2.in start → power3.out landing per-particle, arrival times staggered left-to-right across the glyph — same 'front sweeps across the shape' schedule as particle-text-dissolve's per-cell 'at' value — so the hook reads as a fast, directional snap, not a mush). By the 0.5s beat the dot-matrix 'MG' (Inter Black 900, grid-sampled) is fully converged and crisp. [0.50-1.40s] Hold target_mg positions exactly (zero drift while settled — legibility floor of 0.3s comfortably exceeded at 0.9s) with one GLOBAL alpha-multiplier breathing pulse (sine, ±8%, one full cycle across the hold) — a collective shimmer, never per-letter or per-particle independent flicker. Begin easing off target_mg in the final ~0.1s to hand off into morph-swarm.

scenes.emotion: pattern-interrupt — energy spikes, one clear shift
scenes.motion: The single change for this piece: each particle i interpolates from target_mg[i] to target_bubble[i], NOT along a straight line — add a shared deterministic turbulence offset (a fixed-seed sum-of-sines field, e.g. offset=(k1*sin(f1*t+phase_i), k2*sin(f2*t+phase_i+1.3)) with small fixed k1/k2, so the field reads as fluid/turbulent, never random-per-frame) so the swarm visibly liquifies rather than morphing glyph-to-glyph. At the 1.4s handoff both per-particle speed AND the global alpha multiplier spike briefly (~1.15x) to sell the interrupt, then ease down (power2.out) as particles approach target_bubble[i], with outline-flagged particles (outline_flag_i=true) arriving slightly ahead of fill particles so the silhouette reads before the interior fills in.

Particles lock onto target_bubble[i] on-beat at 2.3s (hard arrival, not a lingering ease, to land the 'snap' feel): outline-flagged particles render at #c4b5fd / ~90% opacity and fill particles at #a78bfa / ~45% opacity, denser on the outline exactly as designed so the rounded speech-bubble + tail (WhatsApp-silhouette proportions) stays legible at small README width. Hold crisp for the full second (legibility floor exceeded ~3x over) with one soft brightness pulse through ONLY the outline particles — #a78bfa→#c4b5fd→#a78bfa, one cycle — as the single 'alive' cue, like a message just landed. Fill particles and position stay static through the hold.

scenes.emotion: exhale — gently resets, no jarring cut
scenes.motion: Every particle i eases from target_bubble[i] back toward scatter_i + drift(i,t) (ease power2.inOut), outline particles dimming from #c4b5fd back to the ambient #a78bfa and the global alpha multiplier relaxing from the settled bubble level down to the scatter ambient (~25-30%). Because drift(i,t) is a periodic closed-form function with period == duration_s, the field's state at t=3.8 is mathematically identical to its state at t=0 (see particle_system.loop_closure) — no eyeballed match, no flash, no snap-to-black, no new color introduced. The MP4 loop reads as continuous ambient drift rather than a restart.
